Retreating to the entrance of the B3 chamber, he pauses, silently looking back at the dark equipment area — the transmitter's indicator light is fully out, the control panel gathering no reflection in the boundless darkness, utterly silent. He firmly notes the precise position of the cut cord and the anomalous trace, lingers no longer, and steadily retraces his route to the surface.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His fingertip lightly presses the edge of the iron box, verifying the trace) The power cord was precisely cut... the sealing tape intact, yet the box was shifted by someone. This method of traceless power-off and covert finishing — it's Ito.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Transmitter, complete. Chapter Six Archive Fragment 5/9 unlocked. The power cord precisely cut late at night; the slight shift of the iron box; the method exactly matching Ito's earlier style of traceless file-clearing and covert alteration in the library, identifying the covert operator.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Shen Mo does not withdraw directly by the shortest route; he pauses midway in the dim B1 corridor, stopping before the stone wall covered in number carvings. In the darkness, with no need for light, he verifies by memory alone the position, order, and depth of every carving, confirming that all past marks are intact — no covering, no alteration, no new traces from outsiders.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Once confirmed, he raises his hand, slightly curling his fingertip, and with his nail gently scratches a new short stroke beside the existing carvings on the wall. The new mark is shorter and shallower than all past marks, low-key and restrained; its position, spacing, and depth strictly follow the chronological pattern of the past marks, fitting the overall sequence perfectly with nothing abrupt. Having made the mark, he lingers no longer, turns and steadily withdraws along his route, reaches the underground hidden door, and gently closes the panel from inside. The hinge, worn smooth by long use, makes no sound; the door closes flush, traceless and seamless.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His fingertip has just left the new short-stroke carving) This one is shorter and shallower than Father's. The mark on the door frame outside the hidden door, the original carving at the B3 entrance... three marks in one line, father and son of one blood. This web — I've completed it for Father.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Mark, complete. Chapter Six Archive Fragment 6/9 unlocked. Three carvings align in a full line; the father-son inherited mark sequence runs in one vein; the underground trail closes into a complete loop.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: In the early hours, Shen Mo quietly returns to the counting house. No lamp is lit inside; it is sunk in still darkness. Su Wan has not slept; she sits alone on the low stool by the stove, silently waiting for his return, her posture steady, her expression calm — no anxiety, no fear. Shen Mo sits silently at the table; in the darkness he deftly takes out the ledger, precisely turns to the page for November 15, and lightly touches the paper, confirming the lining is intact and the hidden object is safe. The moment he gently closes the ledger, heavy, orderly footsteps sound from the street outside — the regular march of a Japanese patrol formation, far exceeding the scale and force of routine patrols. The whole formation suddenly halts at the mouth of the alley, holding in place for a moment; the atmosphere tightens abruptly. Inside, the two remain motionless, holding their breath, letting the risk circle outside. After a moment, the footsteps sound again — not entering the alley, not approaching the counting house — heading straight away along the lane.

preDialog.speaker: Su Wan
preDialog.text: Someone stood at the mouth of the alley for a while.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: ...They've passed?

preDialog.speaker: Su Wan
preDialog.text: They didn't enter the alley. They paused at the mouth, then turned and left.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (He gently places the ledger in the drawer, not locking it) The one that halted at the alley mouth was a Japanese special patrol detachment... yet it did not search deeper. Ito, you already removed my name from that file late on the night of December 7.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Yamada's Search, complete. Chapter Six Archive Fragment 7/9 unlocked. The Japanese patrol halted briefly at the alley mouth with no intent to search deeper; Ito completed the file sanitization late at night, classifying Shen Mo's entry as unrelated to the library, covertly removing suspicion and fully clearing the short-term risk.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Before dawn breaks, Shen Mo goes alone to No. 72 Dixiwei Road. The study door on the third floor is still ajar; a gentle push opens it, the hinge smooth and silent, with no sound of disturbance. The desk and furnishings inside remain as they were; the desk's hidden compartment is still open, exactly as when he last visited.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: His gaze falls on the desk, where he clearly sees a new, faint impression. The impression is not deep, its outline regular — the bottom mark left by a thin old book resting for a long time; after the book was taken away, the trace remained, faint but discernible. Following the direction of the impression, he reaches out and finds the hidden groove on the side of the desk against the wall — the groove is deeper than before, with clear fresh traces of being reopened and pressed. The groove is empty — no paper, no object, no residue. His fingertip lightly brushes the dust distribution inside the groove; its thickness, density, and points of deposit all follow a pattern, clearly confirming that this place was recently opened and used, and the object taken away was deliberately cleared and restored.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: He stands before the desk, neither searching nor probing the other corners, disturbing not a trace of the scene. Before leaving, he verifies the carving on the inner side of the door frame — the original mark is intact, with no covering, alteration, or new marks by anyone. Once confirmed, he gently closes the study door, walks slowly down the stairs, leaves the No. 72 residence, and departs quietly.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His fingertip hovers, not touching the traces) A new mark on the desk, the hidden compartment reopened, the groove deliberately emptied... Father, before you left Shanghai, you came back and took the last thing. In early December, you arrived before me.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Shen Shi'an's Traces, complete. Chapter Six Archive Fragment 8/9 unlocked. The new book mark on the desk; the traces of the hidden compartment's second opening; Father's covert return to No. 72 in early December, taking the last core object, then finishing early and clearing all remaining clues.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: In the early morning light, Shen Mo walks steadily into the Lu Lu Tong Teahouse. The door of the second-floor private room is half open; inside sits a man in his thirties, wearing a plain grey cloth gown, a cup of clear tea before him untouched, his posture upright, his expression calm, as if he has been waiting a long while. Shen Mo pushes the door open and closes it behind him, shutting out the noise of the streets. The man rises and reaches out to shake hands; Shen Mo does not raise his hand in response, but sits directly across the table, gently pushing the teacup to the center of the tabletop, then takes the 1938 Concession map from his inner pocket and spreads it flat on the table.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: Those puzzles in the old Lu Lu Tong site were fully set up in the spring of 1941. The people have passed through; the puzzles remain there. Now only one node has yet to fall into place.

preDialog.speaker: Pan Hanyu
preDialog.text: That node is no longer in Shanghai.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: I know.

preDialog.speaker: Pan Hanyu
preDialog.text: You know where he is. Can you walk the whole road alone?

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: Yes.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: The man raises his hand and moves the teacup to the corner of the table, walks toward the door, his fingertip on the handle, turns back and asks one final question in a low voice, then pushes the door open and leaves. Morning light floods in through the door gap, laying a long narrow band across the threshold. Shen Mo rises right after him and, following the direction of the light, walks slowly out of the private room and down the stairs. The teahouse staff downstairs have already resumed work, moving tables and chairs, sweeping the shop; the street, silent for days, finally regains a hint of its former life.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Pedestrians grow more numerous on the street, their steps hurried; the newspaper stand reopens, and the whole city barely revives after the upheaval. Shen Mo pays no attention to the bustle. At a crossroads he stops, takes the old map from his inner pocket, and turns it over. In the blank space on the back of the map, a line of pencil writing is clearly revealed: December 7, 1941. He is waiting for you. The handwriting is unfamiliar — not any hand he knows — yet its finishing strokes are from exactly the same source as the numbered marks on the edge of the old newspaper at the Lu Lu Tong Teahouse, one vein running through both.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (He folds the map and tucks it into his inner pocket) December 7... on the same day I transmitted core intelligence late at night, Father left Shanghai, transiting through Vladivostok on his way to Moscow. He left; the puzzles stayed here. This web — at last it is fully woven.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Pan Hanyu, complete. All Chapter Six archive fragments 9/9 unlocked. Combining every technique, the ultimate loop of all the clues is closed: on December 7, 1941, the same day Shen Mo transmitted core intelligence late at night, Shen Shi'an successfully evacuated Shanghai, transiting through Vladivostok on his way to Moscow, covert and traceless throughout, escaping cleanly.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: When Shen Mo walks out of the teahouse, a man stands at the foot of the stairs. Grey suit, no sidearm. Behind him stand two in plain clothes, both below the stairs, not following up. The man in grey speaks: Shen Mo. Shen Mo stops. Yamada. The two are five steps apart. Yamada holds a file; Shen Mo recognizes the cover.

clearDialog.speaker: Yamada
clearDialog.text: Your name is in it. Page three. But I'm not sure why it appears on that page.

clearDialog.speaker: Yamada
clearDialog.text: One of my men changed this entry for you. I couldn't find out who. But I know you're not alone in there.

clearDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
clearDialog.text: Then why are you here?

clearDialog.speaker: Yamada
clearDialog.text: I came to confirm you're not worth arresting.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Yamada is silent for a long time, then turns and walks down the stairs. At the last step, he says that one line. He leaves; the two in plain clothes follow. The teahouse staff don't know what happened and keep wiping the tables. Shen Mo stands at the top of the stairs on the second floor, his fingertip touching a folded map — Father's road. His road. Now aligned. He walks down the stairs and heads toward the street corner. Without looking back. — He came to find you. He left. He chose it himself.

hiddenStory.speaker: Narrator
hiddenStory.text: The nine archive fragments of Chapter Six assemble into one complete web. The identity check in the morning light, the anonymous intelligence note, the 1938 map of the concession, the teacher's original puzzles left behind, the transmitter silenced without a trace, the inherited father-son carvings, Ito's sanitization of the file, Father's covert return... Shen Mo has walked his father's road to its end, and woven this web to its close.

hiddenStory.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
hiddenStory.text: (His fingertips trace the folded map) My father's road. Ito's road. My road. They are aligned now. The web is woven — and it is time for a man to set out.

epilogue.speaker: Narrator
epilogue.text: Chapter Six · The Web, complete. The thunderclap of Pearl Harbor lands; the era of Shanghai's lone island draws to a close. Yamada's Tokkō investigation file is quietly sanitized by Ito, and Shen Mo's father, Shen Shi'an, has already slipped out of Shanghai in the deep night of December 7, transiting through Vladivostok on his way to Moscow. The final door of the storeroom hidden amid the chaos closes silently in the boundless dark. Chapter Seven · Finale · The Storeroom is already in sight.

epilogue.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
epilogue.text: (Standing by the counting-house window, gazing into the eastern light) Through all the drift and fall of these times... she still keeps a lamp burning for me. Chapter Seven · The Storeroom... I'm coming.

chapters.title: 第七章·库房（1941年12月·上海至远洋）

prologue.speaker: Narrator
prologue.text: The thunderclap of Pearl Harbor lands; the era of Shanghai's lone island ends for good. The whole city falls under martial law, the streets held in a tight grip, the Japanese blockade impenetrable — the city sinks into a night of grim silence and crushing control. After Shen Mo takes the final intelligence from the Lu Lu Tong Teahouse and completes every covert trail of Chapter Six, each lingering question settles, each planted seed closes its loop. Yamada's Tokkō investigation file has long since been quietly marked sanitized by Ito, stripping him clean from the list of suspects. His father, Shen Shi'an, closed out every clue ahead of time and slipped out of Shanghai in the deep night of December 7, transiting through Vladivostok on his way to Moscow. The teacher's original puzzles, laid out over a lifetime, sit shelved and sealed in the old Lu Lu Tong site. And the transmitter line beneath the archive library has been cut with surgical precision — a clean, deliberate incision, the traceless hand of someone closing the books.

prologue.speaker: Narrator
prologue.text: The board of the times has been set; every move laid in advance has reached its end. The final door of the storeroom hidden amid the chaos closes silently in the boundless dark — and Shen Mo stands awake outside it, never drawn in, never caught in the game, only retracing every path in silence as he waits for the last road ahead to settle.

prologue.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
prologue.text: (Standing still in the night, retracing every path) Every door, every road, every mark, every game... they all deserve an ending now. The door of the storeroom — I'm coming.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: At the deepest hour of the night, Shen Mo leaves the heart of Shanghai one final time. He has walked this route alone twice before — through the unnoticed back lanes of the French Concession, across the silent footbridge over Suzhou Creek, along the abandoned railway tracks heading west. Twenty minutes later, he stands beneath the shadow of the abandoned western-suburbs warehouse. He does not approach the main entrance immediately; instead, he stops outside the perimeter wall and carefully surveys the entire structure. No new openings. No fresh climbing marks. No signs of recent contact. Everything remains exactly as it was — silent, untouched, undisturbed. Only after confirming the surroundings does he slip through an old gap in the side wall and enter the warehouse grounds.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: At the center of the warehouse floor lies a large washed-out area. The water mark is broader and deeper than before, covering the exact location where the iron case once stood. The original trace has been completely erased. Shen Mo does not linger. He does not search the empty ground. He simply follows the outer wall, returns to the entrance point, and crouches beside the old doorframe.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: At the base of the frame, a brand-new vertical scratch catches his attention. Its direction matches perfectly with the exclusive mark he left at the Archive Library back door in April. The line is straight. The pressure is firm. The cut is precise. But it was not made by his hand. Shen Mo's fingertip stops a fraction above the scratch. He does not touch it. Instead, he studies it from the air alone, memorizing its depth, width, angle, and pressure pattern.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His fingertip hovers above the scratch, not touching it) A vertical scratch... same origin as my exclusive mark, but different in form — deeper pressure, wider grain. This mark was made by another hand.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Western Suburbs Warehouse, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 1/9 unlocked. Shen Mo has fully identified the mark's owner: this final scratch was made by Ito — after cutting the transmitter power line and completing the invisible cleanup in the dead of night, he came specially to the western-suburbs warehouse to leave this last hidden trace, sealing the entire covert game with a closing signature.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: At first light, before the frost has melted, Shen Mo returns to the old residence at No. 72 Dixiwei Road. The third-floor study remains exactly as he left it. The door is slightly open. The hinges move smoothly. Nothing inside has changed. The desk remains in place. The hidden compartment is still open. The groove beside the wall is empty. No new object. No displaced item. No fresh trace. Shen Mo stops at the doorway. He does not enter. He does not touch anything. Only with his eyes does he inspect the entire room — no intruder, no alteration, no added clue, no missing evidence. Everything remains unchanged. Satisfied, he turns and walks downstairs.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Halfway down the staircase, a faint sound comes from the first-floor wooden door. Not a knock. Not a movement. Only the quiet tremor of a door panel being gently pushed shut. The sound echoes clearly through the silent morning. Shen Mo's pace does not change. He continues down the remaining steps. At the end of the first-floor corridor stands Mrs. Zhou. She has clearly been waiting for some time. One hand rests lightly against the doorframe. Her back remains calm and still. Without turning, she speaks.

preDialog.speaker: Mrs. Zhou
preDialog.text: Your father left something with me before he departed. He said — if one day he returns, give this to him.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Shen Mo stops midway down the corridor. He does not approach. He simply waits. Mrs. Zhou slowly opens her hand. An old envelope rests on her palm — the paper yellowed, the corners worn, the seal intact. No opening. No tear. No sign of damage. Shen Mo takes it. Only then does Mrs. Zhou turn. Her eyes meet his — a moment of examination, recognition, relief. Then everything returns to silence. She withdraws her hand, turns, and disappears into the shadow behind the staircase.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His fingertips brush the intact seal of the envelope, never opening it) The envelope entrusted by Father... the seal is perfectly intact — unopened, undamaged. Before he left, he came back specially to this room that had been sealed for three years.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: No. 72 Dixiwei Road, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 2/9 unlocked. The envelope's transfer was fully controlled, with no third party handling it; the core clue inside remains complete and intact, with no substitution, loss, or tampering.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Beneath the gray morning sky, Shen Mo returns alone to the old bookshop on Avenue Joffre. The door that once concealed countless secrets is now firmly sealed from outside. A brand-new iron lock hangs in place. The wooden panels are tightly joined. No gap. No light. No sign of movement within. Shen Mo stands before the entrance. He does not push the door. He does not test the lock. He does not crouch to search for the old hidden key beneath the windowsill. He only observes — the lock model, the mounting position, the latch structure. Every detail is recorded silently. No forced entry. No tampering. No passage.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: The moment he turns to leave, something catches the edge of his vision. Inside the windowsill, on the old bookshelf panel, lies an extremely faint short-stroke mark. Its direction matches exactly with the exclusive signal he created in June. But the execution is different. The pressure is almost restrained to nothing. The cut is shallow. Far lighter than any previous mark. A signal made not to demand attention, but only to exist. Shen Mo pauses briefly. He does not approach. He does not verify it physically. He simply remembers it. Leaving the place where he once obtained the hidden book, he finally places the last endpoint he has spent half a year reconstructing. Beside the old windowsill mark, he leaves a single line of pencil-written coordinates — a clear address, a final destination.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (His gaze lingers briefly, without stopping to investigate) A short-stroke mark... the pressure is almost restrained to nothing, the cut shallow — a signal deliberately subdued. The final address is placed in its original position. This long game should come to its close.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Old Bookshop on Avenue Joffre, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 3/9 unlocked. The windowsill address remains intact — unmoved, uncovered, with no new pointing trace. The entire hidden clue chain closes cleanly, leaving no loose end.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: In the quiet afternoon, Suzhou Creek flows slowly beneath the gray sky. Shen Mo walks to the Fourth Bridge. He does not cross. Instead, he descends the old stone steps beside the river and sits near the water. The current moves gently against the bridge pillar. The sound is low and steady — different from the chaos of December's earlier days. The river is calmer now. Fallen leaves drift sparsely across the surface. Shen Mo takes out the yellowed envelope from inside his coat. He does not open it immediately. He places it quietly on his knee. Beside it, he unfolds the 1938 French Concession map. His eyes move to the hidden address written on its reverse side. Every character remains exactly as he remembers. No change. No error. No alteration.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: The opposite bank is empty. No boats pass. No pedestrians appear. Only the sound of water and his own breathing remain. After a long silence, Shen Mo finally opens the envelope. Inside is a neatly preserved letter. The paper edges are intact. No tear. No crease. Only one restrained line of handwriting appears: "Mo — I am your father. I left not because I did not wish to wait."

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Reading it through at a glance, gathering all his emotions) My father's handwriting... "I left not because I did not wish to wait." The signing date is December 8 — the very day I completed the final transmission of the core intelligence in the dead of night.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Suzhou Creek, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 4/9 unlocked. My father's handwriting, the hidden address, and the withdrawal route — three threads converge into one. All the farewells foreshadowed and hidden trajectories are fully closed, and the road ahead is clear and certain.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Before dawn fully arrives, Shen Mo reaches the Huangpu River wharf. The river is open beneath the morning sky. No dense fog. No violent waves. No gathered fleet. Only several freighters and passenger ships resting quietly offshore. He walks slowly to the end of the jetty and stands there. The wooden planks beneath his feet are worn by years of wind and water. Their faded surface carries the marks of time. The morning light spreads across the river. Small reflections shimmer on the water. Clear. Quiet. Unobstructed.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: After confirming the route environment, Shen Mo turns toward the wharf office. He asks only what is necessary. No unnecessary questions. No mention of destinations beyond what is required. No search for companions. No attempt to investigate. He simply purchases a ticket. The destination printed clearly: Vladivostok. He stores the ticket safely inside his coat — together with the father's letter, together with the old map. The pieces now confirm one another.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Pausing one last time at the end of the jetty, gazing at the open river) Vladivostok... exactly matching my father's withdrawal route, the direction marked on the letter, and the sea route preserved in my mother's photograph. Three generations of hidden paths finally converge on the same direction.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: Vladivostok, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 5/9 unlocked. The route is set, the direction certain — identical to the path taken by the previous generation. All scattered clues finally converge into a single road ahead.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: In the soft morning light, Shen Mo returns once again to the familiar counting house. It has been only a day since he left. When the door opens, the room remains peaceful. Safe. Unchanged. Su Wan sits alone beside the stove on the low wooden stool. The white porcelain bowl on the windowsill remains where it has always been. Its opening faces east — their final and most familiar peace signal. Seeing him return, Su Wan does not stand. She does not ask where he has been. She does not show surprise. She simply lifts the lid from the pot, serves a bowl of warm congee, places it quietly on the desk, then returns to her seat beside the stove.

preDialog.speaker: Su Wan
preDialog.text: When are you leaving?

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: ...Tomorrow.

preDialog.speaker: Su Wan
preDialog.text: The ticket has been bought.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
preDialog.text: ...Yes.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Standing still for a moment, speaking softly) The congee was warm. Every concern, every thought, every farewell left unspoken — all of it remains between us. The white porcelain bowl on the windowsill faces east, steadily guarding the final peace and expectation.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Counting House, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 6/9 unlocked. The white porcelain bowl on the windowsill steadily faces east; the peace signal remains. The warmth and steadiness of companionship in a turbulent age are all preserved here, becoming the firmest foundation for the road ahead.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: In the early mist, the ferry begins to move. The ropes are released. The engine deepens. The vessel slowly separates from the Shanghai wharf. Shen Mo stands beside the rail. Morning sunlight falls from the east, resting quietly on his shoulder. Behind him, Shanghai gradually disappears. The foreign buildings along the Bund. The bridges crossing Suzhou Creek. The endless warehouse roofs beside the river. One by one, they fade into the mist. Their outlines soften. Their distance grows. Until the entire city becomes only a gray shadow.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Shen Mo stands motionless. He does not hold the railing. He does not wave goodbye. He does not look back. Inside his coat are everything he carries from the past: his father's handwritten letter, his mother's old photograph, the teacher's unfinished puzzle fragments, the 1938 French Concession map. Every clue. Every memory. Every unfinished responsibility. All preserved. All completed.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Raising his eyes toward the direction ahead) My father's handwritten letter, my mother's old photograph, the teacher's puzzle fragments, the 1938 map... every clue is safely stored. Shanghai is left behind.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Ship, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 7/9 unlocked. The ferry steadily sails northeast, precisely toward Vladivostok — the route exactly matches the withdrawal paths taken by his father and mother in their time. Three generations of journeys and perseverance find their ultimate echo at this moment.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: After leaving Wusong Mouth, the ferry enters open water. The river merges with the sea. Layers of fog drift across the deck, then gradually thin. Behind the ship, a long white trail spreads across the water. Slowly. Quietly. It dissolves into the waves. Shanghai disappears completely. No skyline. No harbor. No trace.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: Shen Mo steps onto the deck. The sea stretches endlessly before him. From behind comes a faint sound. A footstep. Someone stops nearby. Watching. Waiting. Not approaching. Not speaking. Not leaving. Shen Mo does not turn. He does not investigate. His expression does not change. After a moment, the footsteps disappear into the sound of the wind and waves.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Letting the sea breeze brush his face, the fog wrap around him) Someone paused briefly, watching in silence... coming and going without a trace, just like every hidden game of mine in the past. As the fog clears, the direction ahead has become clear.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Fog, complete. Chapter Seven Archive Fragment 8/9 unlocked. The course is constant, the heading unchanged. All the groundwork, all the journeys, all the forbearance steadily advance toward the single final destination.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: The fog finally disappears. Transparent sunlight pours through the cabin window. Every object on the berth is clearly visible. Shen Mo sits at the edge of the bed and slowly lays out the things he has carried with him: the father's handwritten letter, the 1938 French Concession map, the outbound ticket, the teacher's remaining puzzle fragments, the hidden words written on the back of his mother's photograph, the final coordinates left behind by his father.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: One by one. Each object is worn by time. The edges are faded. The paper carries the traces of years, separation, and countless hidden struggles. They appear to be independent fragments. Separate clues. Different moments. Different hands. Yet every path has always pointed toward the same direction. From the very beginning until now, no one forced him forward. No one gave him the entire answer. No one walked the road for him. He discovered every route himself. He verified every mark himself. He completed every loop himself.

preDialog.speaker: Narrator
preDialog.text: He finally understands: the storeroom door that ran through the entire book, always left unresolved, was never a door he needed to force open. He never opened it. Instead, by following every route, solving every clue, and completing every trace, he watched it close naturally. No explosion. No revelation. No final confrontation. Only silence. And that silence was the true ending.

preDialog.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
preDialog.text: (Standing beside the rail, the sea breeze against his face) Every door, every road, every mark, every hidden game — all closed in perfect completion. The storeroom door was never opened, yet it has quietly closed. I have walked it all.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The deck. The sea stretches endlessly. The wind comes from the east. Shen Mo stands for a long time. The evidence in his coat has all aligned. His father's letter. His mother's photograph. The teacher's puzzle fragments. Yamada's file. The direction-finding team's records. He no longer needs to open them to look again. Footsteps sound behind him. One person. Unhurried. Steady. They stop three steps away. Shen Mo does not turn.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: You have walked it all.

clearDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
clearDialog.text: So have you.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: I started earlier than you. But I never truly stopped.

clearDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
clearDialog.text: Ito.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: The vertical scratch at the western-suburbs warehouse — you left it. You left a short stroke; I left a vertical line. Your father's short stroke is in B3. Three generations. Three ways of marking. It took me three years to understand this rule. You took four months.

clearDialog.speaker: Shen Mo
clearDialog.text: You never killed anyone.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: No. I only rearranged things. Files. Routes. Numbers.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: This key is useless now. But keep it. I get off at the next stop.

clearDialog.speaker: Ito
clearDialog.text: You were right. I never truly stayed. You did. That is why you reached the end, while I only passed through.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: He walked into the cabin door. He did not look back. He did not close the door. The key remained on the rail. The sea breeze blew for a while, then Shen Mo reached out, picked it up, and put it in his pocket. The ship continued east. The horizon had no end.

clearDialog.speaker: Narrator
clearDialog.text: The Storeroom, complete. All Chapter Seven Archive Fragments 9/9 unlocked. The final chapter of the book. The story ends. — He walked every road you walked before you. But on your road, he stopped. Then he left. Not defeat. It was simply time to get off the ship.

hiddenStory.speaker: Narrator
hiddenStory.text: The nine archive fragments of Chapter Seven assemble into one complete road home. The final carving at the western warehouse, the letter entrusted by his father, the final address on the windowsill, the letter in his father's hand by the Suzhou Creek, the ticket to Vladivostok, the farewell at the counting house, the old key left on the ship's rail... Shen Mo has walked his father's road to its end, and his own road as well.

hiddenStory.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
hiddenStory.text: (The old key held in his palm) He walked every road you walked before you. But on your road, he stopped. Then he left. Not defeat. It was simply time to get off the ship.

epilogue.speaker: Narrator
epilogue.text: Chapter Seven · The Storeroom, complete. The final chapter of the book. After Pearl Harbor, Shen Mo finishes the last of the closing work — confirming the files, destroying the puzzles, sealing the transmitter. Pan Hanyu confirms at the mouth of the lane that the road has been walked to its end, and Shen Mo steps onto the gangplank that carries him out of Shanghai. Every door, every road, every mark, every game — all closed in perfect loop.

epilogue.speaker: Shen Mo CHIBI
epilogue.text: (Standing on the open-sea deck, the sea wind on his face) The ship sails on eastward. The horizon has no end. The road ahead is already beneath my feet.
